pr_title: Fix Vim 'e' Behavior When Boundary Is Last Point on Line
pr_body:
This was originally just to fix https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/4354, which I did by just returning the previous offset in `find_boundary`.. but `find_boundary` is used in the "insert mode" / normal editor too, so returning the previous boundary breaks existing functionality in that case. 

I was considering a new `find_boundary` function just for some of the vim motions like this, but I thought that this is straightforward enough and future Vim functions might need similar logic too.

Release Notes:

- Fixed https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/4354

- This does not seem to be the case for every language for me.  I was not able to repro this in JavaScript but I was able to in Python.  

- If you press "b" (the opposite motion) it seems to function correctly

One thought here: instead of passing in `false` majority of callsites, is it possibel to add a 2nd method, next to `find_boundary`, and both methods use an underlying method but one of them passes `false` in and the other `true`? That way we don't have to change the existing callsites that much.

Example:

`find_boundary` and (new) `find_boundary_exclusive`, both use a (new) method called `find_boundary_point` (or something) and `find_boundary` passes in `false`and `find_boundary_exclusive` passes in `true`.
